data.name: Mufakhar
data.gender_notes: Mufakhar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic verb 'fakkara', which means 'to strive, contend, or compete'. In Islamic history, the name is associated with several notable figures who exhibited courage and determination in their quests for knowledge and righteousness. The name Mufakhar carries the meaning “Competing, Contending, Striving” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mufakhar usually hope their child will grow to embody competing, contending, striving and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Encouragement to strive in the path of righteousness and seek knowledge and wisdom.
data.etymology: Mufakhar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Competing, Contending, Striving.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mufakhar total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Mufakhar ibn Dhul-Jawshan, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) who distinguished himself in the Battle of Uhud. He was known for his exceptional courage and piety.
historical_references.time_period: 624-656 AD (11th year of Prophet's mission until his death)

historical_references.reference: Mufakkar al-Din Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Halim, the Ayyubid Sultan of Egypt who ruled from 1240-1248 AD. He is known for his military campaigns against the Crusaders, particularly his successful siege of the Crusader fortress of Kerak in 1244 AD.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Mufakhar remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
